title: Choose the dashboard's visual world
question: The roll assigned the Tide Gauge. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Content and wording stay exactly as they are; only the look and arrangement change.

options.label: Tide Gauge
options.lineage: harbour tide-gauge staffs, flood-mark plaques and almanac tide tables
options.thesis: The cuff is the tide: pressure rises and drains on a giant enamel gauge, and blood's return is fixed to it like a flood mark.
options.viewport: A floor-to-ceiling gauge staff on the left with the cuff's level draining live; the run as a tide curve to its right; the Now/Watch-for narration stencilled along the bottom as harbour signs.
options.risk: Needs one line saying the water is the cuff; if the water reads as blood, the story inverts.

raised.raise: Gravity sets the reading order: the public screen reads top-down as the level falls.
One fixed scale everywhere: the gauge never rescales between live, result and technical.
Chronology accumulates: each run's flood mark stays on the staff for the day, older ones weathered.
Tabular numerals throughout; the technical view is dense almanac columns, no cards.
States print themselves as lines in the tide log, never as chips or badges.

options.label: Anatomical Atlas Plate
options.thesis: Every run drawn as a numbered atlas plate of the arm: the cuff, the artery, the moment blood returns.
options.viewport: A life-size engraved arm across the screen; the cuff band fills crimson as it squeezes; numbered leader lines carry the narration; the reading lands as the plate's caption.
options.risk: Medical illustration is where most runs for a health subject land, and the engraved drawing is the hardest thing here to make well in code.

options.label: Living Light
options.lineage: bioluminescent plankton wakes in a night sea
options.thesis: The sensor reads light through the skin, so the forearm's signal is drawn as living light that brightens when blood returns.
options.viewport: Black field; the blood-volume trace as a glowing wake crossing the screen; the cuff number large and white; the return marked by a crimson spark.
options.case: Fuses well: light really is the mechanism and a glowing booth screen pulls passers-by in; loses on making the pressure number the hero.
options.risk: Near-black with glowing edges is one of the looks AI interfaces cluster around; it must stay legible from across the booth.

options.label: Glaze Shelf
options.lineage: glaze runs on a kiln shelf
options.thesis: Flow that runs, stops and pools, read in one shelf row.
options.viewport: Each run as a glazed cup on one shelf.
options.case: Fuses poorly: visitors do not connect glaze with blood or pressure.
options.risk: Reads as a craft site, not a measurement.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.lineage: fixed-scale botanical plates through the seasons
options.thesis: The run's phases as plates at one exact scale.
options.viewport: Four phase plates on one baseline.
options.case: Fuses poorly: cream and serif is a default look, and plates slow a passer-by down.
options.risk: Bookish and quiet at booth distance.
options.kept: One fixed scale across every phase.

options.label: Road-Case Stickers
options.lineage: tour road cases buried in stickers
options.case: Declined: nothing is fully legible, which breaks the reading.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: The run as barcode fields and sine lattices.
options.viewport: A strobing field of bars with one sine trace.
options.case: Fuses for judges only; passers-by get spectacle, not the story, and crimson has no place.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.thesis: The run as a scrolling transcript.
options.case: Declined: a costume of a tool, and text-only loses the passer-by.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean clinical monitoring dashboard: white cards, KPI tiles and line charts, done impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Pressure tile and run timeline on top, three narration cards below.
canonCard.risk: Close to what the dashboard is now, the look you said reads as AI-generated.
